director.chapterArc: Tactical instruction shifts to chaotic combat; Toren's confidence turns to catastrophic error, followed by a physical collapse and Wyck's revelation of passive power. The scene resolves in exhaustion and a hard lesson on the gap between knowing rules and executing them under fear.
director.restraintNote: Maintain an analytical distance throughout. Do not dramatize the violence; describe it as mechanical consequence. Toren's internal panic must be felt through rhythm, not volume. Wyck's revelation is delivered with quiet shock, not triumph. Rook's final lesson is a tired truth, not a lecture.

cues.delivery: Instructional and precise. Rook's voice is flat but carries absolute authority; treat the description of Stilts as a tactical briefing rather than horror exposition.
cues.from: "Stilts, is what I call them. They stand about as high as me, and about nine-tenths of it is leg. Two legs, jointed backwards, longer than they've any business being, and a body slung between them no bigger than a dog, and a head you won't be able to find and won't need to. Colour of wet ash, same as the hounds, same as everything.
cues.through: "Stand where the trees are. Never stand at the end of a row. If you find yourself looking down a long clear stretch of anything, you are already in the wrong place, and you should move before you finish the thought."
cues.reason: Establishes the rules of engagement through calm instruction.

cues.delivery: Accelerate rhythm slightly. Toren's internal monologue becomes urgent; the action is described with clinical speed.
cues.from: Toren's whole spine went cold, and his mouth was already moving.
cues.through: Toren caught that part in pieces, out of order, and had to sort them afterward. Rook's weight had already gone onto the forward foot before the hound cleared the hedge. The light came out along the outside of his right forearm and took its edge on the way, from the wrist outward, the way a crack takes across ice. Then the arm went across at hip height. Once. Level. Without hurry.
cues.reason: Transition from training to first contact.

cues.delivery: Observational and grounded. Describe the orchard setting with a steady, rhythmic cadence that contrasts the coming violence.
cues.from: He did not say anything else. Toren walked the next two miles with his ears ringing and his chest about four inches further out than it had started the morning, and every step of those two miles laid down a little more of the thing that was going to cost them at four o'clock.
cues.through: Along the bottom, between the lowest row and the creek bank, ran a stone-lined ditch, four feet deep and as straight as the rows. Somebody had cut it to carry creek water west to the press-house, with maybe a foot of fall in the whole two hundred yards. The lining stones stood on edge, frost-lifted now and leaning; the coping had gone in places; the bottom held silt and a standing crop of nettles that came up to the lip and no higher. From anywhere above the second row it showed only as a seam in the hillside — a line of nettle-tops, and nothing under them.
cues.reason: Set the scene before the tactical deployment.

cues.delivery: Rapid-fire calls. The dialogue should feel like a drill; precise and efficient.
cues.from: "Third row, two of them, third row!" — Dessa, from the steps, clear and hard.
cues.through: Then the row discipline worked, and it worked so well that it was almost boring.

cues.delivery: Staccato and physical. Describe Wyck's kill as a mechanical action; Toren's error is described with immediate self-criticism.
cues.from: He let it come inside the trunks and inside the length of the bar. The knee of its left leg jointed backwards, the way they all did; he did not swing against the bend, he swung with it, two hands, low and flat, the whole weight of his shoulders going through the middle of the bar into the joint. The joint went the way it already wanted to go, and then further than it wanted to go. The leg folded. The creature came apart downward, all its height arriving on the ground at once, like a stepladder coming apart.
cues.reason: Show the mechanics of combat and the first failure.

cues.delivery: Shift to urgency. Toren's realization is internal but frantic; the call from Dessa cuts through with sharp clarity.
cues.from: He stood in the third row with his heart going and a warm spike in his fist and thought: we're doing it. We're actually doing it.
cues.reason: The turning point: the ditch breach.

cues.delivery: Fast and fragmented. The retreat is a 'controlled fall'; the formation of the line must sound like practiced instinct.
cues.from: "Down!" Rook shouted, from somewhere up the slope. "Everyone west — press-house — now, go, go—"
cues.through: They killed two on the apron.

cues.delivery: Rook's action is described with impossible precision; the pause at the ditch mouth must feel like a sudden freeze-frame.
cues.from: Rook took the second one in the air.
cues.through: Toren saw the point of its right foot set into the clay. He saw the little ridge of pushed turf standing up in front of it, where it had loaded. He looked straight at it.

cues.delivery: Toren's panic peaks then snaps into a release. The Ember activation is described as 'world went very simple'—clinical and terrifying.
cues.from: Toren's whole spine went cold. The cold came with a name already on it. The name was a gift. It was the wrong gift, and it was his.
cues.reason: The catastrophic error followed by the power surge.

cues.delivery: Sudden collapse. Toren's exhaustion is physical and absolute; Wyck's intervention is described with heavy, grounded impact.
cues.through: The last one came out of the ditch at Wyck and did the same thing and got the same result.
cues.reason: The aftermath of the error and Wyck's revelation.

cues.delivery: Quiet and intimate. Rook tends to the wound; Wyck's voice 'comes apart' slightly.
cues.from: The ash ran down the apron and pooled in the dished places where sixty years of cart wheels had worn it, and Rook let it lie for eleven minutes, which nobody had ever seen him do, because he was working on Wyck's arm.
cues.through: "I can't do anything," said Wyck, and his voice came apart slightly in the middle of it, which was the first time Toren had ever heard that happen. "I haven't got anything. I'm fifteen and nothing, ask the woman with the book, she wrote it down. I just don't —"
cues.reason: The debrief begins with a focus on physical reality.

cues.delivery: Rook's explanation is delivered with quiet gravity. The concept of 'passive Ember' must sound like a hard truth.
cues.from: Rook let go of the arm.
cues.through: "They'll never put you in a book for it. You can't show it to anybody. You can only be it, and you have been being it since before I met you, and it's the least impressive and most useful thing on this hillside."

cues.delivery: Toren's physical state is described with hollow exhaustion. Rook's reassurance is practical and devoid of false comfort.
cues.from: Toren could not stand until nearly dark.

cues.delivery: Rook's debrief is rhythmic and measured. The final lesson must land with a sense of shared burden rather than blame.
cues.from: The debrief was that night, in the lee of the windbreak, with the lamp on the cart shaft and all five of them where he could see them.
cues.through: "That's all it bought. That's what it was for. On the bridge you were wrong for as long as it took a girl to get three hounds out of a treeline, because you had no other picture in your head to fall back on. Tonight you had one, and you didn't believe it fast enough, and you were wrong for two seconds instead of four, and the difference between two and four is why he's got a forearm, and she's got a leg that limps.

pauses.after: "So don't watch them. Watch the lines."
pauses.reason: End of the core tactical instruction; let 'Watch the lines' land.

pauses.after: Toren had gone to sleep with his hand on a warm stone thinking that this was the easiest thing anyone had ever asked him to remember.
pauses.reason: Transition from training confidence to the journey's start.
After Rook confirms Toren's call; a moment of quiet validation before the walk.
Toren asks where Rook is standing; pause for the answer and the tension it creates.

pauses.after: "Two in the row, one at forty," Toren said after him, and got the spike out.
pauses.reason: After Toren gets the spike out; a breath before combat begins in earnest.

pauses.after: She said it in a completely different voice from the one she had been using, and it went across the orchard like a thrown stone.
pauses.reason: Dessa's call of 'Ditch' is a major shift. Let the horror and urgency sink in.

pauses.after: The first came straight up the middle. Milo called it at thirty feet. Toren set his feet the way he had been made to set them four hundred times. He did not go to meet it. The spike went in under the body as the body arrived. The thing's own weight finished it. The same weight put Toren flat on his back with a wasp-smelling mat of grass in his ear.
pauses.reason: After Toren kills the first Stilt; pause before Rook's impossible move.

pauses.after: Toren's whole spine went cold. The cold came with a name already on it. The name was a gift. It was the wrong gift, and it was his.
pauses.reason: Toren realizes his mistake. The 'wrong gift' needs time to register as a fatal error.

pauses.after: He put it through the first Stilt lengthwise, in under the body and out through the far shoulder of it, and did not slow down for the resistance, because there was no resistance. The second one came off the steps at him with its point already set. He took both legs off it on the backswing, at the same height, one pass, and neither of them touched the ground before he had turned for a third.
pauses.reason: After the Ember surge; pause before the physical collapse hits.

pauses.after: He should have. Nine stone of boy, and a thing that had crossed forty feet in no time at all, and it came off him the way water comes off a gatepost. Wyck's boots stood exactly where Wyck's boots had been standing. The clay under them did not even give.
pauses.reason: Wyck absorbs the impact. Let the impossibility of his survival register with the listener.
Rook reveals Wyck's passive Ember. This is a major character revelation requiring silence to process.

pauses.after: "Yes," said Rook. "And he's face down in the windfall and you're sitting up, so let's neither of us pretend that settles anything."
pauses.reason: After Rook dismisses the comparison between Toren and Wyck; pause before the physical reality of Toren's state returns.

pauses.after: "Because you turned the line for two seconds," he said, "instead of four.
pauses.reason: Rook explains the two-second difference. Let the math of survival land.
